name: Fat Gripz / grip thickeners

card.summary: Thick rubber grip sleeves sold for forearm work; one acute study exists, none on forearm size.
card.note: No long-term data on forearm thickness.

quick.overview:
Fat Gripz wrap around a bar to make it thicker so the hands and forearms work harder when holding it. They are marketed for forearm thickening.

Only one acute study on strength and muscle activation was found; forearm growth has not been tested in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: A thicker handle reduces how well the fingers can wrap around it, increasing the demand on the grip muscles.
quick.risks: No adverse effects were documented in the sources reviewed.

lead: Fat Gripz are thick rubber sleeves that slip over a barbell, dumbbell, cable attachment or handle to increase its diameter, making it harder to hold. Lifters use them to give the forearms and hands more work, and many add them to curls and pressing to chase bigger-looking forearms and arms. [1][2]

The maker, Fat Gripz Enterprises, markets them as a way to build bigger, stronger arms by recruiting more muscle fibres per rep and to raise grip strength so more weight can be handled on other lifts; it sells three diameters, about 4.5 cm, 5.7 cm and 7 cm. [2] Those are the company's own claims.

One acute study examined the effects of fat grip attachments on strength and muscle activation in resistance-trained men. [1] Grip strength references list thick-bar holds among methods for training the closing grip. [3] No long-term trial of forearm or arm size has been found.

chain: Thicker handle reduces how well the fingers wrap the bar
Hands and forearm flexors work harder to hold on
Greater forearm demand; users also report a stronger arm pump
angle.text: Lifters add the sleeves to farmer's holds, curls, rows and wrist curls so the forearms get more work, with the goal of thicker forearms and stronger grip.

infobox: About 4.5 cm, 5.7 cm and 7 cm outer diameter [2]

paras: The sleeves are made of a dense rubber compound and fit over standard bars, dumbbells, cable attachments, machine handles and bands. The brand sells a smaller size for lighter grip or smaller hands, a mid size that it recommends for most goals, and a larger extreme size. [2]

On T Nation, lifters log fat-grip versions of curls, dips, bench work, farmer's pickups and wrist curls. One poster wrote that they can turn anything into an axle and described them as good for elbow health; another said they gave an even bigger arm pump during a triceps block; others log forearm blocks of wrist curls with the sleeves. [4][5][6][7]
A strongman logger noted a practical trick of placing them over band attachments so knurling does not wear them. [8]

A study in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research examined the acute effects of fat grip attachments on muscular strength and neuromuscular activation during resistance exercise in resistance-trained men. [1] Details of its results were not available in the material reviewed. No longer-term trials on forearm thickness were found.

lore.intro: Thick-grip sleeves come up in lifting logs and gear threads as a way to hit the forearms and add an arm pump.

claims.claim: Thick grips grow bigger forearms and arms
claims.believers: The brand says it builds bigger arms by activating more fibres, and T Nation lifters describe heavier forearm work and a bigger pump with the sleeves. [2][5]
claims.experts: One acute study measured strength and muscle activation; no trial has measured forearm or arm size. [1]

claims.claim: Thick grips are good for elbow health
claims.believers: One T Nation poster described them as amazing for elbow health. [4]
claims.experts: No published study in this area was located.

claims.claim: Thicker bars raise grip strength so other lifts improve
claims.believers: The brand states that grip strength increases allow more weight on other exercises. [2]
claims.experts: Grip references list thick-bar holds among closing-grip training methods. [3]
